source_correspondence: H0–H1 state the compact scalar coefficient family, possibly indefinite tangential principal form, nonradial glancing anchors, common incoming window, bounded compressed band and whole-input source product condition. The geometry precedes the target order.

G0 computes the scalar normal gauge with its exact sign and full conjugated tangential operator. All complex lower terms remain. The gauge acts on mixed Sobolev spaces, while the original Banach norm is retained without an invariance assumption.

L0 preserves the actual zero Dirichlet value. L1 explicitly isolates the earlier coarse-graph construction that needs no transverse root separation; a proper tangential inverse followed by the complete boundary source tree controls the first normal derivative.

S0 retains the complete ratio-kernel commutator of the original equation before the gauge. Tested cutoff errors are elliptic in the transition band even for an indefinite tangential form. Moving the one input normal derivative onto the regularized output uses the proved ordinary H2 estimate, with every pre-domination source family retained.

S1 justifies uniform use of the earlier constructions for bounded auxiliary families of full kernels. Uniform diagonal choices use the supremum of the finitely many seminorms required at each stage. No differentiable extension of the damping parameter through zero is assumed.

O0 keeps a finite quantitative chain of half-order gains. Nested regions have the same final endpoint, every incoming and source norm is retained, and direct induction produces the displayed finite constants. The argument does not deduce an estimate from an all-orders regularity assertion.

O1 converts all incoming norms to actual boundary operator families using the complete mixed compressed-band calculus. O2 constructs one fixed observation parametrix and retains its full residual. That residual is controlled through the original equation and its complete source tree.

A0 recovers the original targets, retaining both target residuals and the gauge. A1 forms the entire finite union before exact scalar Fourier domination. Every source input support and angular margin remains inside the explicit source product patch.

A2 identifies the actual tested-graph completion by flat transposed kernels. It does not assume graph density or global multipatch assembly. External human foundations remain explicit and internal CC0-export closure is unclaimed.
Three complete solutions verify the complex normal gauge, eleven finite half gains and all coordinates of an indefinite-form Hamilton trajectory. Twenty-three exact checks support the analytic proof.
